title: HackIllinois 2026
text:
HackIllinois 2026

HackIllinois is the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign's premier collegiate hackathon. Prospective attendees can register by the priority deadline on January 4, 2026 to be entered into a raffle to win an iPad, or the final deadline on January 27, 2026.

Participants can work individually or in teams to submit projects to a specific track for a chance to win prizes. Whether you're a beginner or an experienced hacker, HackIllinois offers workshops, mentorship, and an inclusive environment for everyone to learn and create.

### Who is eligible to attend?

HackIllinois is open to all current college students and recent graduates (within 1 year of graduation). You do not need any prior coding experience - we welcome students of all skill levels! Whether you are a beginner or an experienced hacker, there is a place for you at HackIllinois.

### Where is HackIllinois located?

HackIllinois 2026 will be held in the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. We'll provide more detailed location and parking information closer to the event date.

### Will overnight hacking space be provided?

Yes! HackIllinois will provide overnight hacking space for attendees this year. This dedicated space allows you to work on your project throughout the night in a safe environment.

The LLVM Foundation is committed to diversity and education in the fields of compilers and tools, and supporting the long term health and growth of the LLVM Project. Therefore, the LLVM Foundation provides travel grants to students attending the LLVM Developers’ Meetings or other compilers and tools related educational conferences.

Applications are open for student travel grants to attend the 2026 LLVM Developers’ Meeting taking place October 27 - 28, 2026 (pre-conference sessions on October 26) at the Santa Clara Marriott.

The deadline for 2026 LLVM Dev Mtg applications is July 17, 2026.

The deadline for student grant applications has passed.

Scholarship recipients are selected based on the following criteria:

- Participation with the LLVM Project or relevant work experience.
- Financial need.

- Priority may be given to underrepresented backgrounds, genders, and experiences to encourage broader participation in computer science and engineering.
- Priority may be given to those within the local travel region.
- Past recipients of LLVM Foundation travel grants may not be selected.

title: ATC 2026: The 2026 ACM SIGOPS Annual Technical Conference
text:
ATC 2026: The 2026 ACM SIGOPS Annual Technical Conference

## ATC 2026 Student Scholarships and Travel Grants

ATC 2026 offers a limited number of grants to help full-time undergraduate and graduate students attend the conference in Hong Kong. Students may apply whether or not they are presenting work.

Funding is competitive and may cover conference registration and part of reasonable travel and accommodation expenses. Awards may not cover all requested costs.

### Eligibility

Applicants must:

- be enrolled full-time at an accredited institution;
- study computer science, computer engineering, or a related field;
- attend ATC 2026 in person if selected; and
- disclose all confirmed or pending funding for the trip.

Postdoctoral researchers are also eligible.

### Application Materials

Please submit:

- the completed application form;
- a CV of no more than two pages;
- proof of current full-time student status.

Applications will be evaluated based on financial need, relevance to ATC, expected benefit from attending, available institutional support, and contributions to broad participation.

text:
The 2026 ACM SIGMOD/PODS Conference: Bengaluru, India: Student Travel Grants

# SIGMOD 2026 Student Travel Grants

Thanks to the generous support from SIGMOD and other sponsors including the National Science Foundation, we will provide scholarship awards to selected students attending the SIGMOD/PODS conference. The scholarships will include financial support for traveling. 

Each awardee will receive a stipend to partially cover the expense to attend the conference. The amount will be determined based on the availability of funds and the number of granted stipends. Awardees are expected to register to the main conference and will have to make their own arrangements for travel and accommodation. 

## Eligibility

Applicants need to be a full-time student (undergraduate,graduate or PhD). 

Applicants are eligible to apply for the SIGMOD travel award even if they have submissions under consideration at other events at SIGMOD, such as the Undergraduate Research Program, or the New Researcher Symposium. However, an applicant cannot receive more than one travel award in total. 

Applicants do not need to have an accepted paper to be eligible. However, students who are primary authors of an accepted paper in the main conference or the workshops are especially encouraged to apply. Junior students without papers accepted for publication at SIGMOD/PODS, but involved in research closely related to the topics of the conference are also encouraged to apply.
